spec_match.rationale: The block half is exactly right (measured edge gaps, sibling gap untouched, real margin-trim declarations), but the page offers inline / inline-start / inline-end values that the current css-box-4 grammar (none | block | [ block-start || block-end ]) no longer defines, and demos them on a display:flex container that margin-trim does not apply to — the ChromeStatus summary scopes Chrome 155 to block and multicol containers.

interactive.rationale: Value buttons with aria-pressed, a margin slider, an inline-flow toggle, a generated rule, and a three-row measured-gap table that re-renders on every input.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises 'switch between block and inline flow to see which edges each keyword actually affects', which is built on the dropped inline half of the grammar.

edge_cases.rationale: margin:0 ('no margin to trim') and the unsupported branch are handled, but in inline/flex mode the end-edge measurement reads leftover free space (48px measured here) rather than a margin, so the number cannot mean what the row label says even where trimming worked.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5197863732772864, the css-box-4 margin-trim section and MDN.

conformance.rationale: The block-behaviour assertions are excellent (rendered-box measurements, sibling-gap preservation, single-edge scoping), but the suite also asserts the inline values parse — see the flag below; those assertions look wrong against the current spec grammar and the shipped scope.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: banner honestly reports margin-trim unsupported; block value measured 16/16/16 not-trimmed with accurate narration; inline-flow toggle switched the axis, rule and measurements (16 / 32 between / 48 free-space end); console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Every render logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('trim-measured', …) with the value, measured gaps and support flag.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, pressed value buttons swap background and color, visible amber padding band makes the trimmed edge legible, 44px targets.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled slider and checkbox, aria-pressed value buttons, captioned measured table with scoped headers, aria-live narration.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP (the inline-flow row scrolls internally by design); both screenshots clean.

openQuestions.title: Drop or rework the inline mode: the values are out of the spec and the container is the wrong kind
openQuestions.detail: The current css-box-4 draft defines margin-trim as none | block | [ block-start || block-end ] and states it applies to block containers and multi-column containers with no effect on inline-level descendants; the ChromeStatus entry for this feature likewise scopes Chrome 155 to block and multicol. The explorer's inline / inline-start / inline-end buttons therefore offer values Chrome 155 will not parse, and its inline mode applies them to a display:flex container, which margin-trim does not apply to at all — so on a real 155 the inline half would 'measure the same as none' while implying browser immaturity rather than an invalid demo. Additionally the flex end-edge measurement reads unfilled row space, not a margin. Rework the mode to a genuinely spec-covered case (e.g. block-start/block-end on each edge separately, which the page already supports) or annotate it as historical grammar. The feature index's API sample (.tags { margin-trim: inline; }) carries the same stale value.

openQuestions.title: Flag: conformance inline assertions look wrong against the shipped spec (human only)
openQuestions.detail: FOR A HUMAN, per the immutable-conformance rule — nothing was edited. In v155/margin-trim/conformance.json, margin-trim-inline-parses asserts CSS.supports('margin-trim','inline') and margin-trim-single-edges-parse requires inline-start and inline-end to parse. The current css-box-4 grammar contains no inline keywords and ChromeStatus scopes the Chrome 155 ship to block containers + multicol, so these assertions would plausibly stay red forever even on the shipping build — indistinguishable in the rollup from a genuine regression. Chromium 141 cannot arbitrate (everything fails here); please verify on a real Chrome 155 and correct the suite if confirmed.

summary: Half excellent, half stale: the block-axis explorer is a model measured demo (verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless — cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp — at http://localhost:3000/v155/margin-trim/trim-explorer/, with an honest unsupported banner, 16px untrimmed gaps narrated correctly, clean console and zero overflow both classes), but the inline half demos grammar the spec has dropped, on a flex container the property does not apply to, with an end-gap number that measures free space. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 7 fail — honest here, but the two inline parse assertions are flagged as likely wrong against the shipped scope.
